answer: Every identity starts a solo voyage with zero credit. Let trust grow like a grove: each epoch of graded work adds a ring, each honest attestation adds a root, and roots only entangle with identities that kept showing up. Grants, votes and grading seats are priced by that growth, not by headcount. A farmer steering a fleet of fakes into the inlet discovers each hull must pay fresh compute every epoch just to float, yet still carries sapling weight: no rings, no roots, no yield. Cost per fake identity stays linear in heads and time, while one deep-rooted account outearns the whole fleet.
